changelog: **Relation shapes, the data foundation (#1804, slice 1):** `MentorshipRelation.relationType` (`ONE_TO_ONE` default | `GROUP` | `PEER` | `REVERSE` | `FLASH`; whitelist in client-safe `src/lib/relationShapes.ts` — a different question from `kind`) and the new child model `RelationParticipant` (relationId, userId, role `MENTOR|MENTEE|FACILITATOR`, `isPrimaryPair`, `joinedAt`, `leftAt`; `@@unique([relationId, userId])`). Purely additive: `mentorId`/`menteeId` stay non-null and stay the pair's truth. Seats that mirror the pair (`isPrimaryPair`) grant nothing — a mentor corrected in place can never keep access through a stale row — while seats beyond the pair grant membership until `leftAt` is stamped (a seat is never deleted). `src/lib/relationParticipants.ts`: `isParticipant()`, `memberIdsOf()`, `participantsOf()`, `mentorsOf()`, `menteesOf()`, `writePairSeats()`, `addSeat()`, `leaveSeat()`. Authorization moved to it in `GET /api/mentorship/[id]`, the relation thread (`getThreadIfAllowed`) and `loadAccessibleMeeting`; a thread post and the typing signal reach every current member (`threadRecipients()`). One active mentor (#419) now counts an open MENTEE seat too (`findActiveMentorship`), so a group's mentee cannot also hold a one-to-one. The shared create path writes the pair's mirror seats; a duplicate-account merge moves seats; the insert-only backfill `0036-relation-participants` (`prisma/backfill-relation-participants.mjs`, also on topic deploys) seats every existing relation and is a no-op on re-run.
